audit_notes: Slip: measured hydrodynamic slip of water on smooth hydrophobic surfaces (incl. PDMS brushes) is 10-30 nm (Vinogradova, Bocquet & Charlaix); liquid-like brushes reduce contact-angle hysteresis (drop mobility) but not hydrodynamic slip by orders of magnitude. Adjusted effective_slip_length 5e-8 -> 2e-8 m; b+ = 0.004 -> expected gain 0.02%: no meaningful drag change. Pillar height 150 nm = 0.03 viscous units -> hydraulically smooth; nanopillars wet fully under hull pressure (Laplace pressure of a 20 nm gap would be ~MPa, but the brush-coated pillars are only mildly hydrophobic, so no stable nano-plastron is assumed). Structural: silica-siloxane pillars ~50 nm wide, aspect ratio ~3: bending under 50 Pa shear negligible (stress ~kPa vs GPa strength); risk is abrasion-induced fracture of the pillar array by sand/ cleaning, and fouling-conditioning films (proteins, dead cells) covering the pillars within days, which neutralises the mechano-bactericidal effect. The benefit is antifouling, not drag, and cannot be computed here. Baseline: smooth FR, slip 0.
